question: Which layer should own the fix after a current v0.6.12 reproduction: upstream OpenClaw Copilot device polling, Windows wizard-session handling, or both?
rationale: The Windows app renders a gateway-controlled wizard, while the observed direct CLI behavior points toward upstream authentication; only a real current setup can establish the failing boundary without creating duplicate logic.

options.title: Reproduce and route
options.body: Run the current bundled CLI and Windows wizard flows, capture gateway and CLI diagnostics, then assign the fix to the layer that fails to observe authorization completion.

options.title: Route upstream now
options.body: Treat the direct CLI transcript as sufficient evidence of an upstream OpenClaw auth defect and track only Windows-side recovery UX here.

options.title: Close as historical
options.body: Close only if maintainers can provide current-head proof that completion, expiration, credential activation, and restart-free chat all work.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and route
recommendation.body: Run the current bundled CLI and Windows wizard flows, capture gateway and CLI diagnostics, then assign the fix to the layer that fails to observe authorization completion.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent setup triage and release work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for coordinating a bundled-version reproduction across Windows and upstream OpenClaw.
